_note: Curated political tracker. Dates are as reported; where outlets disagree the item says so. Update as events occur.
headline: The reduced parliamentary committee (Diputación Permanente) ratified RDL 29/2026 by 35–34 on 12 Nov, with PNV support, so the 2% cap on rent updates, the eviction moratorium to 2030 and 10% VAT on tourist lets are now law. It rejected RDL 28/2026, so the lease-extension decree has lapsed. A day earlier, Spain held its first general strike over housing since 2012. The campaign opened on 13 Nov. Polls give PP and Vox a combined majority for the 29 Nov election, and the PP has pledged to unwind the controls.

decrees.summary: Ratified 35–34 (PSOE, Sumar, PNV, ERC, Bildu, Podemos for; PP, Vox, Junts against). It caps annual rent updates at 2% to end-2027, suspends evictions of vulnerable households to 2030, adds rules on seasonal and room rentals, and puts 10% VAT on tourist lets from 1 Dec. A new government could repeal it.
It got only 34 votes after PNV voted no. Automatic lease extensions and the move to open-ended contracts are gone. Tenants who asked for an extension while it was in force face legal uncertainty.
Allows rent caps in tensioned zones (Catalonia first; others vary by region). The PP has pushed motions to repeal it, so a PP-led government could unwind the caps.

timeline.title: Housing Law (Ley 12/2023) in force
timeline.detail: Lets regions declare 'tensioned zones' with rent caps based on reference indices, and adds extra limits on large landlords.

timeline.title: Catalonia applies first tensioned-zone rent caps
timeline.detail: First region to use the 2023 law; 140 municipalities are covered.

timeline.title: Government proposes 100% tax on non-EU non-resident buyers
timeline.detail: Announced as part of a 12-point housing plan. It was never voted on and stalled when parliament was dissolved.

timeline.title: Golden visa scheme abolished
timeline.detail: Ends residence permits granted for property investment of €500k or more.

timeline.title: Single short-term rental registry mandatory
timeline.detail: Tourist and seasonal lets need a registration number to be listed on platforms.

timeline.title: Congress rejects both housing decrees
timeline.detail: PP, Vox and Junts voted against. Reported votes: 178–172 and 184–166. The 2% cap on rent updates lapsed.

timeline.title: Mass protests in Madrid and ~50 cities
timeline.detail: Triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old Madrid tenant, who later died in hospital. Tenants' unions call for a general strike.

timeline.title: Sánchez calls snap election for 29 November
timeline.detail: Parliament dissolved about nine months early, with housing as the central issue.

timeline.title: Decrees re-approved as RDL 28/2026 and RDL 29/2026
timeline.detail: Published in the BOE on 7 Oct and in force from 8 Oct. They cap annual rent updates at 2% to the end of 2027, let tenants extend leases ending before 2029 by up to 2 years, ban evictions of vulnerable households to 2030, and add 10% VAT on tourist lets from 1 Dec if ratified.

timeline.title: Permanent rental supply down 10% y/y
timeline.detail: idealista reports that seasonal lets are now about one third of the rental market, a sign of landlords moving away from regulated leases.

timeline.title: PP housing plan: 3 laws in 100 days
timeline.detail: Promises a Land Law, a law against squatting with 48-hour evictions, and a horizontal-property reform. Also pledges 1M homes over the legislature and tax breaks for landlords who extend leases below inflation.

timeline.title: Government pledges tougher rules if re-elected
timeline.detail: Says it will intervene 'with the full force of the law' and points to a €7bn State Housing Plan to 2030.

timeline.title: 8,300 'seasonal' listings ordered off platforms
timeline.detail: The Consumer Affairs ministry is targeting holiday lets disguised as seasonal rentals.

timeline.title: idealista: rents +5.6% y/y in October, −1.1% q/q
timeline.detail: Rents are still rising in 48 of 50 provinces. Huesca leads (+12.1%) and only Gipuzkoa and Álava are falling.

timeline.title: Forcadell / UB: sales to fall ~8% in 2027
timeline.detail: Prices up slightly more than 10% in 2026, with growth easing below 5% by end-2027.

timeline.title: General strike over housing
timeline.detail: The first general strike over housing since 2012, called by CCOO, UGT and tenants' unions. Organisers claim up to 5 million took part; independent reports describe tens of thousands at the marches, with incidents and arrests. Tenants' unions announced a new cycle of mobilisations.

timeline.title: RDL 29/2026 ratified 35–34; RDL 28/2026 rejected
timeline.detail: PNV was decisive after Junts voted no. The 2% rent-update cap, eviction moratorium and tourist-let VAT are now law, and automatic lease extensions lapse.

timeline.title: Campaign opens; manifestos published
timeline.detail: PSOE: state housing company, public housing above 6% of stock, interest-free loans up to €50k. Frente Amplio (Sumar): expropriate homes from large funds, limit investor purchases. Vox: more land, lower taxes, 'national priority' for housing aid.

polls._note: Figures as reported by pollsters and aggregators; blank = not reported. Sumar runs as Frente Amplio in some polls. The CIS is an outlier with PSOE ahead.

parties.housing: Keep RDL 29/2026 (2% rent-update cap to end-2027, eviction moratorium, tourist-let VAT). Manifesto: state housing company, public housing above 6% of stock, interest-free purchase loans up to €50k; €7bn State Housing Plan to 2030.
Runs as Frente Amplio. Proposes expropriating homes from large funds, limiting purchases by investors and deep rent cuts. Backed both decrees.
Its vote ratified RDL 29 on 12 Nov and sank RDL 28 (open-ended leases).
Voted with PP and Vox to reject the decrees on 2 Oct, citing regional powers.
Land Law, 48-hour squatter evictions, 1M homes, tax breaks for landlords who extend leases below CPI, purchase aid for young buyers. Has previously moved to repeal the 2023 Housing Law.
More land and lower taxes, no rent controls, tough anti-squatting rules. 'National priority': Spaniards first for rental aid and protected housing. Voted against both decrees.

buyer_context.text: Golden visas (residence permits for property purchases of €500k or more) ended on 3 Apr 2025. That removed one channel for non-EU investors, and the drop in non-resident buying since then is the first test of how much demand it supported.

A proposed 100% tax on non-EU, non-resident buyers of resale homes (announced Jan 2025) was never voted on, and it has stalled with parliament dissolved. It is not law, but the uncertainty may itself be deterring buyers.

Cross-check: the land registry (Registradores) counted about 97,300 homes bought by foreigners in 2025, 13.8% of sales. The notarial figures here run higher because they include all foreign nationals who live in Spain.
This shows direct exposure only. A foreign pull-back also affects prices and new-build pre-sales in coastal markets, and those effects are not modelled here.
